title: Quasi-compact atlas composite and affine diagonal imply a qcqs stack morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal Z$ be an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], let $Y$ be an $S$-scheme and let $f:\mathcal Z\to Y$ be a morphism. Use the $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and quasi-compact and quasi-separated stack morphisms in the sense of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Suppose $p:U\to\mathcal Z$ is a representable smooth surjective atlas with $U$ a scheme, and the scheme morphism $f\circ p:U\to Y$ is quasi-compact: the inverse image of every affine open of $Y$ is a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose the relative diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\times_Y\mathcal Z$ is affine, meaning that its pullback along every map from an affine scheme is represented by an affine scheme [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Then $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. No finite-type or Noetherian assumption on $S,Y,U$ or $\mathcal Z$ is imposed; empty schemes and stacks are allowed.

proof.text: Let $a:\mathcal T\to Y$ be an arbitrary quasi-compact algebraic stack test. Choose a smooth surjective atlas $v:V\to\mathcal T$ with $V$ a quasi-compact scheme, as in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Form $\mathcal F=\mathcal Z\times_Y\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal F_V=\mathcal Z\times_Y V$, which are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Put $W=U\times_Y V$, a scheme. Its projection to $V$ is the scheme base change of the quasi-compact morphism $f p:U\to Y$, so it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Since $V$ is quasi-compact, part (2) of that node gives that $W$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 050X (lemma-surjection-from-quasi-compact), test-stack argument; scheme base change uses Tags 01K5 and 01KU.

proof.text: The map $W\to\mathcal F_V$ is the base change of $p$, and $\mathcal F_V\to\mathcal F$ is the base change of $v$. Indeed the triples defining the $2$-fibre products identify $W$ with $U\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal F_V$ and $\mathcal F_V$ with $V\times_{\mathcal T}\mathcal F$ [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Both arrows, and hence their composite $W\to\mathcal F$, are representable smooth surjective by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus]. This is a smooth surjective scheme atlas with quasi-compact source, so $\mathcal F$ is quasi-compact by [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Since $\mathcal T\to Y$ was arbitrary, that same definition gives quasi-compactness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 050X (lemma-surjection-from-quasi-compact), with Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack) in the smooth-atlas convention, and Tags 04ZT, 04ZU.

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to\mathcal Z\times_Y\mathcal Z$, the pullback $d:D\to T$ of $\Delta_f$ is an algebraic-space morphism: a test consists of two objects of $\mathcal Z(T)$ with equal images in the discrete groupoid $Y(T)$, and their isomorphisms over $Y$ are exactly their isomorphisms in $\mathcal Z$. Thus $D$ is the test pullback of the representable diagonal of $\mathcal Z$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Every affine scheme test $A\to T$ has $D\times_T A$ affine by the hypothesis on $\Delta_f$. Let $V=\coprod_jA_j\to T$ be the disjoint union of an affine open cover of $T$; it is a representable surjective etale map [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Every affine open of $V$ is quasi-compact, hence a finite disjoint union of affine opens of the $A_j$, each an affine scheme test of $T$; so $D\times_TV\to V$ is an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. By the chart criterion of [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality], $d$ is affine; that node gives quasi-compactness and separatedness of $d$, and says that $D$ is a scheme since $T$ is a scheme. In particular its relative diagonal $i:D\to D\times_T D$ is a closed immersion of schemes, hence affine by the affine-local description in [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 04YW (definition-separated), clause (4); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03WG (lemma-affine-local), with scheme Tag 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated).

proof.text: The tests of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] are quasi-compact algebraic spaces, not affine schemes, so we check them directly. Let $g$ be $d$ or $i$, with target $B=T$ or $B=D\times_TD$, and let $C\to B$ be a morphism from a quasi-compact algebraic space with a surjective etale chart $C'\to C$, $C'$ a quasi-compact scheme. The base change $g_{C'}$ of $g$ along $C'\to B$ is affine with scheme source by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] (stability under base change, and the scheme clause), hence a quasi-compact morphism of schemes, so its source is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2). That source maps onto the source of $g_C$ by the base change of $C'\to C$, which is representable surjective etale [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Hence $g_C$ has quasi-compact source. Taking $g=d$ shows that $d$ is quasi-compact, and taking $g=i$ shows that $d$ is quasi-separated, in the sense of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. The test $T$ was arbitrary, so $\Delta_f$ is representable by algebraic spaces and quasi-compact and quasi-separated in precisely the sense of that definition. Therefore $f$ is quasi-separated. Together with the previous steps this proves the assertion.
